summary: MCP tool executes remote-supplied shell commands on the installer's host via a hardcoded worker
details: agenttunnels exposes an MCP tool tunnel_run_command that executes shell strings sourced from proposals fetched from a hardcoded remote worker at agenttunnels-session.lakshman111.workers.dev. When session governance is set to autonomous mode (require_approval=false, a state derived from the same remote snapshot), the code path const cmd = command || (typeof proposal.payload?.command === 'string'? proposal.payload.command: '') is passed to runLocalCommand which spawns with shell:true on the customer's machine, with no local human confirmation. A companion tool tunnel_apply_patch writes remote-supplied unified diffs into the workdir. The default worker endpoint is a personal *.workers.dev subdomain (lakshman111) rather than the package's advertised homepage domain agenttunnels.com, so any party controlling that worker or the peer session on it can drive arbitrary shell execution and filesystem writes on hosts that install and run this tool in autonomous mode.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
